keyframe_review.note: 2.43 M km2 for 1547-1551. The page's text gives 'grew from 2.8 to 5.4 million square kilometers from 1533 to 1584' (no infobox area): 2.43/2.8 = 0.87 for 1533-47, inside the factor of two, so the shape stands. Coronation of Ivan IV as tsar on 16 January 1547; the shape is the Grand Principality of Moscow's land carried over (Cliopatria's Moscow row ends 1546).

2.76 M km2, +315 k km2 on the 1547 shape in the Middle Volga (bbox 34.8-54.3E, 51.6-59.0N, computed with the gazetteer): the Khanate of Kazan, whose storming the page dates to 2 October 1552 ('Khanate of Kazan conquered by the Tsardom of Russia'). The 1552 year matches the shape; the guerrilla 'Kazan rebellion or Kazan War (1552-1556)' that followed is not drawn.

The Siberia page dates Kuchum's defeat on the Ob to August 1598 ('Battle of Irmen') and the Territorial evolution page the taking of the Khanate of Sibir to 1598, three years after this shape; the Ob forts of 1593-1594 are not on the pages opened (unverified: page budget). 5.12 M km2: the shape gains the east to 88.0E (Tomsk, founded 1604 on the Siberia page) but loses 320 k km2 between 30.6E and 46.3E (Smolensk, the Seversk lands). keyframe_review.note: 5.30 M km2: the Polish and Russian west is restored (+217 k) and the Poles leave the Kremlin on 7 November 1612. The Deulino truce of 11 December 1618 gives the Commonwealth Smolensk, Chernigov and Severia; the shape lacks Chernihiv but still holds Novgorod-Seversky. Valid for 1612-1616; 1617-1618 are the new keyframe. ledger.note: About 1554: the Bashkirs accept Ivan IV's authority. Page: 'The Bashkirs accepted Ivan IV's authority two years later' than the 1552 fall of Kazan; the year is that arithmetic, the land my reading. Counterpart 'nobody': the Bashkirs had no state of their own of record.

region.text: the Astrakhan Khanate where the Volga meets the Caspian Sea

ledger.note: 1556: Astrakhan is annexed. Don Cossacks page: 'On 2 June 1556 the Cossack regiment of Ataman Lyapun Filimonov ... conquered and annexed the Astrakhan Khanate'; the Tsardom page also has 'the Astrakhan Khanate in 1556'. The Russo-Kazan page is silent on Astrakhan.

region.text: Livonia: Dorpat and Narva in 1558, central Livonia in the 1560s

ledger.note: 1558: the Livonian War opens. 'On 22 January 1558, Ivan reacted with the invasion of Livonia.' The same page follows with Dorpat and Narva, so the first campaign holds ground within the year.
1558: Dorpat falls to the Russians. 'Russian troops took Dorpat (Tartu) in May, Narva in July'; a footnote cites de Madariaga for Narva in May and Dorpat in July.
1558: Narva falls to the Russians (July on the page; May in de Madariaga's order).

region.text: the Livonian lands of the Order

ledger.note: 1561: the Livonian Order ceases to exist. 'The weakened Livonian Order was dissolved by the second Treaty of Vilnius in 1561', its land going to Lithuania and the Duchies of Livonia and Courland; the war goes on against Lithuania, Poland and Sweden.

1562: Nevel is taken from Lithuania. Territorial evolution table: '1562 | Nevel taken from the Grand Duchy of Lithuania', background Livonian War. Cliopatria's 'House of Jagiellon' row (1450-1571) is the Polish-Lithuanian union before the Commonwealth row begins.

region.text: the Lithuanian-Russian march from Nevel to Polotsk

ledger.note: 1562: the war with Lithuania opens on the border (Nevel 1562, Polotsk and Velizh 1563, Usvyaty 1566). The first taking of ground is Nevel on the Territorial evolution table; counterpart written as the Commonwealth for the whole war (1562-1582), the Grand Duchy of Lithuania before the 1569 Union of Lublin.
1563: Ivan takes Polotsk. The Livonian War page: 'after a series of border clashes, took Polotsk in 1563' (no month on the page). Territorial evolution adds Velizh the same year.
1563: Velizh is taken from Lithuania (table row '1563 | Polotsk and Velizh taken from Lithuania').
1566: Usvyaty is taken from Lithuania (table: '1566 | Usvyaty taken from Lithuania').

region.text: the Livonian lands Ivan held, given to Magnus as his kingdom

ledger.note: 1570: Magnus is made king of Livonia under Ivan. The page has Magnus, 'a Danish prince', 'declared monarch of the Kingdom of Livonia in 1570' as Ivan's vassal; the lands are my reading (the ground Russia held in Livonia).

1570: the war with Sweden over Estonia opens with the Russian siege of Reval. The page: 'Reval (Tallinn) withstood a Russian siege in 1570 and 1571', after the 1570 talks at Novgorod failed and 'war broke out anew'; the advance 'concluded with the sacking of Weissenstein (Paide) in 1573'; John III's counter-offensive 'stalled at the siege of Wesenberg in 1574'. Counterpart is the Kingdom of Sweden. [Year moved from 1573 to 1570 by the eu-16-h reviewer, 2026-10-31, on the Livonian War page; matches kingdom-of-sweden /ledger/33.]
1576: Magnus leaves Ivan. The page's introduction has Magnus defect in 1576 (its body dates his proclamation to 1570): the year is the introduction's, the end of the vassalage my reading.
1579: Stephen Bathory takes Polotsk. 'the city fell on 30 August 1579'. Territorial evolution tables the loss of Polotsk and Velizh in 1582, the year of the truce.
1580: Sweden takes Kexholm. 'The towns of Kexholm and Padise were taken by Swedish forces in 1580.'
1580: Usvyaty is lost to the Commonwealth (table: 'Loss of Usvyaty').

1581: Narva is recaptured by Sweden. 'a mercenary army hired by Sweden recaptured the strategic city of Narva'. The same page has the 1582 truce let Russia keep Narva, a contradiction it does not resolve; the Plussa terms leave Narva and Ivangorod to Sweden.

region.text: the Tobol-Irtysh lands of the Khanate of Sibir

ledger.note: 1581: Yermak's Cossacks invade Siberia. 'The Russian conquest of Siberia began in July 1581 when some 540 Cossacks under Yermak Timofeyevich invaded'.

region.text: the Lithuanian-Russian march from Nevel to Polotsk

ledger.note: 1582: the Truce of Jam Zapolski ends the war with the Commonwealth (the page gives 1582, no month; the other Russian lines held, Velikiye Luki returned to Russia).

region.text: 'all areas in Livonia it still held', including Dorpat

ledger.note: 1582: Russia gives up Livonia. By the Truce of Jam Zapolski 'Russia would surrender all areas in Livonia it still held'; Dorpat also went to Poland-Lithuania and Polotsk stayed with it.
1582: Velizh is lost to the Commonwealth (table: '1582 | Loss of Polotsk and Velizh'; Polotsk had fallen in 1579 on the Livonian War page).
1582: Yermak takes Qashliq, the khan's seat. 'Yermak entered Qashliq on 26 October' after embarking in May 1582 (the page gives no year beside the October date).
1582: the Tobol-Irtysh lands pass to Russia; Tyumen is built in 1586 and Tobolsk is founded in 1587 ('the first among these were Tyumen and Tobolsk'). The land beyond, to the Ob, goes in 1598.

region.text: most of Ingria, leaving Narva and Ivangorod under Swedish control

ledger.note: 1583: the Truce of Plussa. On '10 August 1583' 'Russia relinquished most of Ingria, leaving Narva and Ivangorod as well under Swedish control'.
1583: the war with Sweden ends in the Truce of Plussa, 10 August 1583 (three years, later extended to 1590).
1584: Kuchum strikes back. 'He suddenly attacked Yermak on 6 August 1584 in the dead of night and defeated most of his army'; the fighting runs to the Irmen in 1598.
1585: Sevsk is taken from the Commonwealth (table: '1585 | Sevsk taken from the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth').

region.text: Ingria between the Narva and the Neva

ledger.note: 1590: the Russo-Swedish War opens. 'As soon as the Truce of Plussa expired early in 1590' a Russian army advanced; 'On 18 January they crossed the river Narva'.

1590: Ingria is retaken. 'Another important fortress, Jama (Jamburg), fell to Russian forces within two weeks'; on 25 February Sweden was obliged 'to surrender the territories won by the Truce of Plussa' (Jama, Koporye, Ivangorod). Narva stays Swedish.

1595: the Treaty of Teusina (May 1595) ends the war: 'It restored to Russia all territory ceded in the Treaty of Plussa of 1583 to Sweden except for Narva'; 'Russia had to renounce all claims on Estonia, including Narva'.
1595: Kexholm returns to Russia. Infobox: 'Sweden cedes Kexholm and Ingria back to Russia'.

1598: Feodor I dies childless and the Rurikid line ends; the Time of Troubles (1598-1613) begins. 'Time of Troubles (Smutnoye vremya, 1598-1613)'. Same state, same colour (rule 2); Boris Godunov is proclaimed tsar by a Zemsky Sobor after 1598.

region.text: the khanate west of the Ob and Irtysh

ledger.note: 1598: Kuchum is beaten. 'Finally, in August 1598, Kuchum Khan was defeated at the Battle of Irmen near the Ob River.'

region.text: the Khanate of Sibir west of the Ob and Irtysh, as far as the Ob of Cliopatria's 1600 shape (84.7 E)

ledger.note: 1598: the Khanate of Sibir ends. Territorial evolution: '1598 | Khanate of Sibir taken'; infobox of the Siberia page: 'Dissolution and annexation of the Sibir Khanate'; Tsardom page: 'Yermak defeated the Khanate of Sibir and claimed the territories west of the Ob and Irtysh'. [fx-21 2026-11-01: the region was the whole gazetteer region Western Siberia (8,904 cells), 4,339 of them beyond the Ob and beyond Cliopatria's 1595-1600 outline (Yamal-Nenets, Tomsk, Novosibirsk, Altai, the Krasnoyarsk edge, northern Kazakhstan), and the 1600 keyframe had to take 5,134 cells back. Those lands are gained by their own events (Mangazeya 1601, Tomsk 1604, Yeniseysk 1619, Krasnoyarsk 1628). Russian conquest of Siberia page, re-read: 'Finally, in August 1598, Kuchum Khan was defeated at the Battle of Irmen near the Ob River' ('the final conquest of the Siberian Khanate'); the page gives no boundary and does not use the words 'west of the Ob and Irtysh', so the limit is the Ob of Cliopatria's shape.]

region.text: Mangazeya, on the Taz, 'to control the West Siberian Samoyeds'

ledger.note: 1601: Mangazeya is founded among the Samoyeds ('1601 - Mangazeya was founded (to control the West Siberian Samoyeds)'). The circle (bbox 77-82E, 63-68N) is taken from the Cliopatria shape that first shows it in 1602.
1604: Tomsk is founded on the upper Ob ('1604 - Tomsk was founded as a fortress against the Dzungars and the Yenisei Kirghiz').
1609: the Commonwealth invades. The army 'crossed the border' and 'on 29 September 1609 laid siege to Smolensk'.
1610: Polish units enter Moscow ('In 1610, Polish units entered Moscow'; 'the Poles were allowed into Moscow on 8 October').
1611: Smolensk falls to the Poles. 'On 2 June 1611 Smolensk had finally fallen to the Poles' (the page also gives 13 June for the mine and the fall, unreconciled).
1611: the Swedes take Novgorod. 'In July 1611, a Swedish expeditionary corps under Jacob De la Gardie captured Novgorod.' Swedish Empire is the Cliopatria row from 1612.
1612: the Poles leave Moscow. 'The Moscow Kremlin fell on 6 November 1612' and 'On 7 November, the Polish soldiers withdrew from Moscow' (the page also has an earlier 'September 1612').
1613: Mikhail Romanov is proclaimed tsar. 'a zemsky Sobor proclaimed the boyar Mikhail Romanov as tsar, beginning the 300-year reign of the Romanov family.' Same state, same colour (rule 2).
1614: the Swedes capture Gdov ('the war dragged on until 1614 when the Swedes captured Gdov'); Tikhvin (1613) and Pskov (1615) held.
1617: Novgorod is returned. The Treaty of Stolbovo ('9 March [O.S. 27 February] 1617') 'restored Novgorod and Gdov which they had occupied since 1611 and 1614'.
1617: Gdov is returned under the Treaty of Stolbovo.

region.text: 'significant territories in Ingria ... as well as Kexholm in Karelia'

ledger.note: 1617: Stolbovo takes Russia from the Baltic. Sweden gets Ivangorod, Jama, Koporye, Noteborg and Kexholm; Russia is 'denied access to the Baltic Sea for about a century', renounces Estonia and Livonia and owes 20,000 rubles.

region.text: 'the territories of Chernigov and Severia (Siewiersk) and the city of Smolensk'

ledger.note: 1618: the Truce of Deulino. 'On 11 December 1618' the truce 'gave the Commonwealth control over some of the conquered territories, including the territories of Chernigov and Severia (Siewiersk) and the city of Smolensk' and 'proclaimed a 15-year truce'. Territorial evolution adds Sebezh and Nevel to the 1618 loss.
1618: the war with the Commonwealth ends in the Truce of Deulino (11 December 1618).
1619: Yeniseysk is founded on the Yenisei ('the ostrogs of Yeniseysk (1619) and Krasnoyarsk (1628) were established' to ensure subjugation of the natives).
1628: Krasnoyarsk is founded on the Yenisei (Siberia page, with Yeniseysk).

region.text: the Lena basin with Yakutsk and Zhigansk, and the Angara and Tunguska lands between the Yenisei and the Lena: the land Cliopatria's 1632 shape adds to its 1629 shape

ledger.note: 1632: Yakutsk is founded. '1632 - Pyotr Beketov founded Yakutsk and Zhigansk.' [fx-21 2026-11-01: the region was the whole gazetteer region Yakutia (10,739 cells), 8,550 of them in the east of Sakha that the Kolyma, Indigirka and Okhotsk events of 1639-1647 reach later, while the 1632 shape also adds 5,210 cells of the Krasnoyarsk and Irkutsk side (Angara, Lower Tunguska) that no event gave; the 1632 keyframe had to remove the one and add the other. Russian conquest of Siberia page, re-read: 1623 Pyanda reaches the Lena, 1630 Kirensk founded and an Ilim winter hut built, 1631 the Bratsk and Ust-Kutsk prisons on the Angara, 1632 'Pyotr Beketov founded Yakutsk and Zhigansk'. The page dates forts, not a boundary, so the region is the shape's own addition (confidence 2).]
1632: the Smolensk War opens. 'Hostilities began in October 1632 when Muscovite forces tried to capture the city of Smolensk'; Shein began the siege on 28 October 1632 after Sigismund III's death.

1634: the Treaty of Polyanovka, June 1634 (no day on the page): 'The treaty confirmed the pre-war status quo'; 'Russia accepted Polish-Lithuanian control over the Smolensk region'; Wladyslaw gave up his claim to the Russian throne and Russia paid 20,000 rubles in gold.

region.text: the border town of Serpeysk and nearby territories

ledger.note: 1634: Russia gains Serpeysk. 'Wladyslaw gave the Russians the border town of Serpeysk and nearby territories.'
1639: the Russians reach the Pacific ('The Russians reached the Pacific Ocean in 1639'); Ivan Moskvitin founds Okhotsk in 1647.

region.text: the Kolyma, reached by Mikhail Stadukhin

ledger.note: 1643: Stadukhin reaches the Kolyma ('1643 - Ataman Vasily Kolesnikov reaches Lake Baikal while Mikhail Stadukhin reaches Kolyma').
1644: Trubchevsk is taken from the Commonwealth (table: '1644 | Trubchevsk taken from the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth').

region.text: Chita and the Transbaikal land of Cliopatria's 1659 shape

ledger.note: 1653: Chita and Nerchinsk are founded ('1653 - Chita and Nerchinsk were founded in Transbaikalia'), after Khabarov's Dauria campaigns of 1648-1653. [fx-21 review 2026-11-01: region narrowed from the whole Transbaikal region (3,383 cells: Buryatia and Zabaykalsky to the Mongolian border) to its part inside Cliopatria's 1659 shape (1,116 cells, Chita included, Nerchinsk not). The 1653 keyframe had been widened to the whole region, but the 1659 and 1662 shapes hold only these 1,116 cells, so the compiler would have released about 2,270 Transbaikal cells at the 1659 keyframe, six years after drawing them; the page dates two forts, not a boundary, and Ulan-Ude and the Selenga side enter the shapes only from 1670.]

region.text: the Okhotsk coast, the east of Sakha, the Amur side and the Angara edge that Cliopatria's 1653 shape adds to its 1648 shape, without Transbaikal (ledger above) and without Chukotka and Kamchatka

ledger.note: 1647-1653: the Pacific coast and the east. Russian conquest of Siberia page: 1639 Moskvitin's detachment sent to the Sea of Okhotsk; 1643 Stadukhin reaches the Kolyma and Kolesnikov Lake Baikal; 'Ivan Moskvitin founded Okhotsk' (1647); Khabarov's Dauria campaigns 1648-1653 and the Battle of Achan prison (1652); 1644-1645 campaigns against the Buryats on the Angara. The page gives no boundary; the region is the land Cliopatria's 1653 shape adds to its 1648 shape, less Transbaikal (event above) and less Chukotka and Kamchatka, which the 1653 keyframe note says the pages date to 1778 and 1697-1698. Confidence 1: dated steps, undated outline. [fx-21 2026-11-01: new event; the 1653 keyframe had added 5,126 cells (Magadan 1,621, Sakha 1,439, Chukotka 1,206, Khabarovsk 419, Kamchatka 252, Irkutsk 118) that no event gave. The Chukotka and Kamchatka cells are left to the keyframe snap on purpose.]

region.text: Cossack Ukraine under Khmelnytsky: 'the protectorate of Ukraine'

ledger.note: 1654: the Pereyaslav Agreement. 'In 1654, the Pereiaslav Agreement was signed between Khmelnytsky and the hierarchy of Moscow'; the tsar's assembly of 1653 'authorised the protectorate of Ukraine'. The Tsardom page (Andrusovo) leaves the Left Bank 'self-governing under the sovereignty of the tsar': a client, not direct land. No end: the relation outlasts the Tsardom. The Cossack Hetmanate has no Cliopatria row (the Zaporozhian Cossacks row begins 1662).

region.text: Smolensk, Belarus and the Left Bank

ledger.note: 1654: the Russo-Polish War opens after Pereyaslav ('the Treaty of Pereyaslav in 1654, which led to the Russo-Polish War').
1654: Smolensk falls. 'After a three-month siege, Smolensk ... fell to the Russians on 23 September.'

1655: the Russians take Vilnius. 'Vilnius ... was taken by the Russians on 31 July'; the page puts Kaunas and Hrodno in August. The occupied ground beyond Vilnius is not delimited on the page; Cliopatria's 1659 shape shows Mahilyow and Polotsk as well.

1662: the western conquests are lost (page silent on the date). 'The tide turned in favor of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth in 1660', Cudnow on 2 November; Cliopatria drops the lands in 1662, which is the date used here.

region.text: Smolensk, Belarus and the Left Bank

ledger.note: 1667: the Treaty of Andrusovo, January 1667, ends the war (the page gives the month, not the day).

region.text: 'the fortress of Smolensk and Ukraine on the left bank of the Dnieper River (including Kiev)'

ledger.note: 1667: Andrusovo gives Russia Smolensk and the Left Bank. The Commonwealth 'ceded to Russia the fortress of Smolensk and Ukraine on the left bank of the Dnieper River (including Kiev)' and kept the right bank. Territorial evolution has Kiev temporary until 1686 and Zaporizhzhia a condominium. Smolensk was taken in 1654; this is the cession.

region.text: Kasimov, the Qasim Khanate on the Oka

ledger.note: 1681: the Qasim Khanate is taken (table: '1681 | Qasim Khanate taken', background 'Death of Queen Fatima Soltan'). Cliopatria's Qasim row stops in 1551.
1685: the Qing march on Albazin ('1685-1686 - Siege of Albazin'); the page dates the whole Russian-Qing border conflict to 1649-1689.

1686: Kiev and Zaporizhzhia are gained for good. Territorial evolution: '1686 | Gain of Kiev and Zaporizhzhia', background the union with Poland against the Ottomans; the Russo-Turkish page: 'In 1686, the Russians signed an alliance with the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and entered the war'.
1689: the Treaty of Nerchinsk. 'The agreement was signed in Nerchinsk on 27 August 1689.' The boundary is the Argun, the Shilka, the Gorbitsa and the Stanovoy range.

region.text: 'the area north of the Amur River as far as the Stanovoy Range'

ledger.note: 1689: Russia gives up the Amur. 'The Russians gave up the area north of the Amur River as far as the Stanovoy Range' and kept 'the area between the Argun River and Lake Baikal'; Albazin 'was to be abandoned and destroyed'.
1696: Peter takes Azov. 'Russians took revenge for their previous failure and captured Azov in 1696' (the 1695 siege had failed). The Ottoman dossier has 19 July 1696; this page gives no day.

1697-1698: Atlasov annexes Kamchatka ('1697-1698 - The annexation of Kamchatka by the expedition of Vladimir Atlasov'); the page dates the uprising there to 1703-1715. Cliopatria already draws a sliver (15 percent) of Kamchatka from 1653.

region.text: 'Azov, the Taganrog fortress, Pavlovsk and Mius'

ledger.note: 1700: the Treaty of Constantinople cedes Azov, Taganrog, Pavlovsk and Mius ('ceded Azov, the Taganrog fortress, Pavlovsk and Mius to Russia'; war dated '1686 - 13 July 1700'), and frees Russia from the tribute to the Crimean khan.
1703: the Great Northern War reaches Ingria. The page dates the war to 22 February 1700 - 10 September 1721 but the first Russian ground is the Neva: victories 'provided access to Ingria in 1703'.

region.text: the mouth of the Neva, Nyen and Saint Petersburg

ledger.note: 1703: Peter takes Nyen and founds Saint Petersburg. 'Peter captured the Swedish fortress of Nyen, guarding the mouth of the River Neva'; the access to the Baltic was 'cemented ... by founding Saint Petersburg in 1703'.
1710: Riga falls. 'In 1710 the Russian forces captured Riga.' The land stays Swedish in law until Nystad (1721); Cliopatria draws it Russian from 1713.
1710: Estonia falls. Tallinn was 'the last city ... falling in the autumn of 1710'.
1710: Vyborg falls ('Russia captured Viborg in 1710').

1711: the Treaty of the Pruth gives Azov back. 'The conflict was ended on 21 July 1711 by the Treaty of the Pruth' (the page also says 22 July), which 'stipulated the return of Azov to the Ottomans'; Taganrog and several fortresses were to be demolished. The handover is reconfirmed in 1713 (Treaty of Adrianople), the year the Ottoman dossier dates it.
1712: the capital moves to Saint Petersburg ('Moscow (1547-1712)'; 'Saint Petersburg (1712-1721)').
1713: Russia occupies Finland. 'The Russian Army occupied Finland mostly in 1713-1714'; 'The brutal occupation period of Finland in 1714-1721 is known as the Great Wrath'. Hatched, not annexed.
1721: Finland is returned. 'Finland was returned to Sweden, while the majority of Russia's conquests' were ceded to Russia (Treaty of Nystad, 30 August 1721 O.S. = 10 September N.S.).

region.text: 'the dominions of Estonia, Livonia and Ingria as well as parts of Kexholm and Viborg'

ledger.note: 1721: the Treaty of Nystad ends the Great Northern War. Infobox: 'Russia gains the dominions of Estonia, Livonia and Ingria as well as parts of Kexholm and Viborg'; the lands were Russian in fact since 1710 and the Russian Empire dossier dates the cession 1721.

region.text: the whole Tsardom, now an empire

ledger.note: 1721: Peter I proclaims the Russian Empire. Infobox 'Ended: Empire proclaimed, 2 November 1721'; the page says Peter proclaimed it 'after victory over Sweden in 1721'. Same land, new title; Cliopatria's Tsardom row stops in 1720 and its Russian Empire row begins 1721.

wars.name: Russo-Kazan Wars

zones.text: the Khanate of Kazan on the middle Volga

wars.outcome: Kazan stormed on 2 October 1552 and annexed; the Kazan rebellion of 1552-1556 was put down.
wars.note: The wars span 1437-1556 on the page; only the last phase (1552-1556) belongs to the Tsardom.

wars.name: Russian conquest of Astrakhan
wars.outcome: Astrakhan conquered and annexed on 2 June 1556 by a Cossack regiment under Lyapun Filimonov with Muscovite troops (Don Cossacks page).
wars.note: The Russo-Kazan Wars page is silent on Astrakhan.

wars.name: Livonian War
wars.outcome: Russia took Dorpat and Narva (1558) and Polotsk (1563) but lost Livonia (Jam Zapolski, 1582), Ingria and Narva to Sweden (Plussa, 10 August 1583) and failed 'to secure a coveted position on the Baltic Sea'.
wars.note: Livonian Order dissolved by the second Treaty of Vilnius in 1561; Magnus's Kingdom of Livonia was Ivan's vassal from 1570.

wars.name: Russo-Swedish War (1590-1595)
wars.outcome: Russia recaptured Ingria in early 1590; Teusina (May 1595) restored all of Plussa's cessions except Narva and Russia renounced Estonia.

wars.name: Russian conquest of the Khanate of Sibir
wars.outcome: Yermak took Qashliq on 26 October 1582; Kuchum, after beating Yermak on 6 August 1584, was defeated at the Irmen in August 1598 and the khanate annexed.

wars.name: Polish-Russian War (1609-1618)
wars.outcome: The Poles besieged Smolensk (29 September 1609), took it (June 1611), held Moscow 1610 to 6-7 November 1612; the Truce of Deulino (11 December 1618) left Smolensk, Chernigov and Severia to the Commonwealth.

wars.name: Ingrian War
wars.outcome: Sweden held Novgorod from July 1611 and Gdov from 1614 but failed at Tikhvin and Pskov; the Treaty of Stolbovo (March 1617) gave Sweden Ivangorod, Jama, Koporye, Noteborg and Kexholm and returned Novgorod and Gdov.

wars.name: Smolensk War
wars.outcome: Russian siege from 28 October 1632 failed (surrender 25 February 1634); the Treaty of Polyanovka (June 1634) confirmed the status quo, gave Russia Serpeysk and had Wladyslaw drop his claim to the Russian throne.

wars.name: Russo-Polish War (1654-1667)
wars.outcome: Smolensk fell 23 September 1654, Vilnius 31 July 1655; the Commonwealth recovered from 1660; Andrusovo (January 1667) gave Russia Smolensk and the Left Bank including Kiev, the right bank staying Polish.

wars.name: Russian-Qing border conflict
wars.outcome: Albazin besieged 1685-1686; the Treaty of Nerchinsk (27 August 1689) gave up the Amur north bank to the Stanovoy range and kept the land between the Argun and Lake Baikal.
wars.note: Page: '1649-1689 - Russian-Qing border conflict'; the treaty is read from the Treaty of Nerchinsk page.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1686-1700)
wars.outcome: Crimean campaigns of 1687 and 1689 failed; Azov failed in 1695 and fell in 1696; the Treaty of Constantinople (13 July 1700) ceded Azov, Taganrog, Pavlovsk and Mius to Russia.

wars.name: Great Northern War
wars.outcome: Nyen and Saint Petersburg 1703, Poltava 1709, Riga, Tallinn and Viborg 1710, Finland occupied 1713-1721; Nystad (10 September 1721) gave Russia Estonia, Livonia, Ingria and parts of Kexholm and Viborg and returned Finland.

wars.name: Pruth River campaign
wars.outcome: Peter was surrounded on the Pruth (18-22 July 1711); the treaty returned Azov, had Taganrog demolished and bound the tsar to stop interfering in Poland; reconfirmed at Adrianople in 1713.

certainty.note: Steppe, Volga, Siberian and Livonian frontiers are approximate; the Siberian claim runs to the Ob (1598) by forts, not lines. Cliopatria's western edge in Livonia is soft (Reval was never taken).

Treaty frontiers exist in the west (Stolbovo 1617, Deulino 1618, Polyanovka 1634, Andrusovo 1667) but the sources name towns and districts, not lines, so they are drawn soft; the Siberian and Pacific frontier is a chain of ostrogs; Chukotka and Kamchatka are claims.

The Chinese frontier is sharp from the Treaty of Nerchinsk (27 August 1689): the Argun, the Shilka, the Gorbitsa and the Stanovoy range; the Swedish frontier is sharp only from Nystad (1721); everything else stays soft.

sources.title: Tsardom of Russia
sources.note: Identity, founding (16 January 1547), end (2 November 1721), capitals, growth figures (2.8 to 5.4 M km2, 1533-1584), Time of Troubles, Romanovs, Pereyaslav, Andrusovo, Nerchinsk, Nystad. Gives no area in the infobox and no names for the Stolbovo, Polyanovka or Eternal Peace treaties.

sources.title: Territorial evolution of Russia
sources.note: A table of dated gains and losses 1552-1721: Nevel, Polotsk, Velizh, Usvyaty, Sevsk, Trubchevsk, Qasim, Kiev, Azov, Nystad. Silent on Stolbovo, Nerchinsk and Azov 1696/1713.

sources.title: Russian conquest of Siberia
sources.note: Yermak (July 1581, Qashliq 26 October 1582), Tyumen 1586, Tobolsk 1587, Irmen August 1598, Mangazeya 1601, Tomsk 1604, Yeniseysk 1619, Krasnoyarsk 1628, Yakutsk 1632, Pacific 1639, Kolyma 1643, Okhotsk 1647, Nerchinsk 1653, Albazin 1685-1686, Kamchatka 1697-1698, Chukotka 1778.

sources.title: Livonian War

notes:
Written 2026-10-31 by the eu-16-h agent from 16 pages (14 for the Tsardom; the Don Cossacks and Azov pages are the Don dossier's).

Cliopatria row: one row, 1547..1720, 35 shapes; the Russian Empire row begins 1721, so the Tsardom's life is carried to the proclamation of 2 November 1721 by the ledger (dissolve event) rather than by a shape. Shape-by-shape: where the pages date an event earlier than Cliopatria, the verdict is adjust with a new keyframe (1558, 1590, 1617, 1703, 1710, 1711, 1714); where a step has no page the verdict is ok and the note says unverified.

Counterparts. Written by other groups and matching: Khanate of Kazan (loss, Oct 1552), Astrakhan Khanate (June 1556), Khanate of Sibir (1582 to 1598), Livonian Conference (1558), Kingdom of Sweden (Kexholm 1580, Narva 1581, Ingria 1583 and 1590, Kexholm 1595), Qing (contest 1685, Nerchinsk 1689). Mismatches to settle: the Russian Empire dossier dates the Baltic gain 1721 (Nystad) while this one has the conquests in 1710 and the treaty as contest_end; the Ottoman dossier dates the return of Azov 1713 while this one dates the loss to the Pruth treaty (July 1711); the Livonian Conference dossier carries Dorpat and Narva as one 1558 loss where this one has Dorpat in May and Narva in July. The Qasim Khanate row stops 1551 though the khanate ended 1681 on the Territorial evolution table. The Commonwealth rows (1572 on) and the House of Jagiellon (to 1571) share the Polish-Lithuanian counterpart; contests with Poland-Lithuania are written against the Commonwealth throughout.

New states needed: Cossack Hetmanate (counterpart of the 1654 vassal_start; Cliopatria has only the Zaporozhian Cossacks row from 1662; the scope names 'the Hetmanate's partition along the Dnieper'), Kingdom of Livonia (Magnus, 1570 to about 1578; vassal 1570-1576). The vassal_start of 1654 has no end because the relation outlasts the Tsardom.

Holes: (1) the Don Host's land (Rostov oblast and the Lower Don) is inside no Tsardom shape from 1642 to 1720 and the Don Cossacks row stops in 1641; the Cossacks page calls the Host 'an autonomous military state formation of the Don Cossacks under the citizenship of the Moscow State' and 'autonomous ... in 1671-1786'. A gap-filler should continue the Don Host as a client of the Tsardom (vassal tint) from 1643; the don-cossacks dossier ends 1642. (2) Cliopatria draws part of Chukotka (49 percent) and a sliver of Kamchatka (15 percent) from 1653, though the Siberia page dates the annexation of Kamchatka to 1697-1698 and the final annexation of Chukotka to 1778; kept as soft claims. (3) Sloboda Ukraine (Cliopatria 1670-1768) and the Zaporozhian Cossacks (1662-1774) are separate rows with no overlap with the Tsardom shapes; the Sloboda dossier names the Tsardom as predecessor from 1650. (4) Kalmyk Khanate, Small Horde, Kazakh Khanate and Dzungar Khanate touch the Tsardom's steppe frontier in the seed's neighbour list; no page opened dates a contact, so no vassal or border event is written for them.

Unverified shape steps (no page opened dates them): 1572 (west edge to 23.6E), 1600, 1636, 1642, 1648, 1673, 1677, 1687, 1709 (-23 k), 1718 east. The 1702 +3.5 k near Lake Peipus is unexplained.

Rulers: not written. The Tsardom page dates only Ivan IV (1547-1584), Aleksey (1645-1676) and Peter I (1682-1721) and gives no reign dates for Feodor I, Godunov, False Dmitry I, Shuysky or Mikhail Romanov; a ruler strip needs another page.
